title: Search a 2D Matrix
summary: Return whether target occurs in the matrix.

contractDetails.constraints: The matrix has 1–100 rows and 1–100 columns. All rows have the same length and are nondecreasing. The first value of each row after the first is strictly greater than the last value of the preceding row. Entries and target are integers in [−10,000, 10,000].

statement: Return whether target occurs in the matrix. Rows are internally ordered, and every row starts above the largest value of the preceding row. Search in logarithmic time in the number of cells.

examples.explanation: The target is the first entry of the second row.
The value falls between the rows.
The final cell contains the target.

hints: Conceptual: Reading across each row in order produces one sorted sequence.
Directional: Binary-search positions in that virtual sequence.
Implementation: With c columns, virtual position i maps to row floor(i/c) and column i mod c.
complexityAnalysis: O(log(rc)) time and O(1) auxiliary space for r rows and c columns. Index arithmetic avoids copying the matrix.
